## Random-survival

### Key parameters
```{r}
#| label: fig-rSFE
#| fig-cap: "Parameter estimates for the rS model. Parameter estimates are organized by category, and include carrying capacity parameters, initial depletion parameters, and mixing parameters. Other parameters include maximum growth rate $r_{max}$, the log variability in annual survival $\\sigma_\\varepsilon^2$, and additional variance parameters for three of the abundance time series. Points are median estimates, while thick and thin bars indicate 50% and 95% credible intervals, respectively."

knitr::include_graphics(here('plots','final','rS Bayes test','Bayes FEs.png'))
```
### Total abundance
```{r}
#| label: fig-rStotabun
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(here('plots','final','rS Bayes test','Bayes total abundance.png'))
```

### Mortality
```{r}
#| label: fig-rSmort
#| fig-cap: "Estimated excess mortality by herd for the rS model. Values represent the estimated number of individuals from a particular breeding/feeding ground combination that died due to variations in natural survival, relative to a baseline survival of 0.96 (@eq-mort). Colored bars are median estimates, while gray bars are indicate the 97.5% quantile of the posterior estimates (i.e., the upper limit of the 95% credible interval)."

knitr::include_graphics(here('plots','final','rS Bayes test','Bayes mortality feed x breed.png'))
```

## Comparison

### Variation in survival estimates
We compared variance parameters $\sigma_{\varepsilon}^2$ (rS, @eq-b8), $\sigma_{\epsilon}^2$ (envS, @eq-b11), $\sigma_{K}^2$ (envK, @eq-b12) to determine whether informing the model with environmental covariates reduces our remaining uncertainty in survival.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sigmacomp
#| fig-cap: "Posterior distributions of unexplained variablity in survival for the three models that estimate time-varying survival."

knitr::include_graphics(here('plots','final','survival variability sigma comparison.png'))
```
### Growth rate
```{r}
#| label: fig-rcomp
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of estimates of maximum growth rate $r_{max}$ by model type. Right panel shows the same data as the left, with the ddOnly model removed for visual clarity."

knitr::include_graphics(here('plots','final','Bayes r comp.png'))
```
### Carrying capacity
```{r}
#| label: fig-Kcomp
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of estimates of carrying capacity $K^b$ by breeding ground and model type. Points are median estimates, while thick and dotted lines indicate 50% and 95% credible intervals, respectively."
```
